newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends firmer, led by March on Brazil talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends firmer, led by March on Brazil talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on Wednesday amid fresh concerns of harvest delays in South American soybean regions, traders said.
"Some were talking about it being too wet in some areas (northern Brazil) and not being able to harvest," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
"Funds were big buyers in meal and beans, something like 3,000 meal was bought and nine million in beans," he added.
A technical move in March soybeans triggered strong fund buying after that contract pierced resistance at $7.50 per bushel, traders said.

Dean Witter reportedly bought six million bushels March, Merrill Lynch bought three million March, Cargill Investor Services bought two million March and Refco Inc bought 1.5 million March and 800,000 May, traders siad.
Still, some were pessimistic after resistance at the recent high of $7.54 proved too strong.
"They couldn't take out fifty-four ($7.54 in March) and that was it. If they take out fifty-four it could have been a great close," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Soybeans closed 5-1/2 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 5-1/2 at $7.50.
Traders continued to talk about dry weather in southern Brazil causing drought-related crop losses and forecasters disagreed on whether rain would hit dry pockets this week.
But Brazilian growers were not yet concerned by the dry weather and did not expect crop losses.

A source at one cooperative in Ibiruba said the crops could withstand another week or two without rain. "Currently we don't consider ourselves to be in a situation of drought," said Paulo Renato Mafsini at the Cotriba cooperative.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 45,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 47,310 contracts.
